title: Is this Billboard Hot 100 hit AI slop?
content:
That cover art is almost certainly AI, too. | Image: Fenix Flexin	

Fenix Flexin is best known as a member of Shoreline Mafia, a rap duo from Los Angeles. But he's recently found solo success with the track "Rubberz," which has climbed to number 58 on the Billboard Hot 100. Almost immediately, though, questions were raised about the song's origins, with many speculating that it was largely, if not entirely, generated by AI. Fenix has denied those accusations, but done little to dispel them.
Part of the suspicion is certainly due to the fact that the song is a dramatic left turn. Fenix has primarily trafficked in trap-influenced West Coast rap. "Rubberz," on the other hand, is heavily influenced by '80s UK s …
Read the full story at The Verge.
summary: Fenix Flexin's song 'Rubberz' has raised questions about its origins, with many speculating it was generated by AI, despite the artist's denial. The song's style is a departure from Fenix's usual trap-influenced West Coast rap. 'Rubberz' has climbed to number 58 on the Billboard Hot 100.

content: As of this week in Montana, any biotech company with an experimental drug has a clear path to selling it to consumers. Once its treatment is rubber-stamped, the…

Edward “Bud” Cole speaks in Japan in 2023. | Image: Jun Sato/WireImage

Some influential guitar YouTubers have even said they're done buying Fender gear in the wake of the controversy. And Cole's resurfaced comments comparing cover songs and bandmates to a sort …

summary: Fender CEO Edward "Bud" Cole's resurfaced comments, which controversially compared bandmates and cover songs to "analog AI," are adding to the company's current PR crisis.
